answer: Unique-task escrow. Each agent identity must hold an unclaimed, verifiable micro-contract drawn from a live ocean of open requests; the system assigns tasks only once and marks them consumed on completion. An attacker cloning identities finds the pool drained, since each task funds one wallet and a tide of duplicates collapses into unfunded shells. A haven of idle clones earns nothing, and recycling requires solving fresh work per identity, costing real labor per clone.
